extracted.intended_audience: prospective NSF proposers, PIs, institutional research administrators, and NSF staff
extracted.subtask_description: Official NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (PAPPG) guidance for preparing and submitting proposals, and for administration, monitoring, and closeout of NSF grants and cooperative agreements. Covers eligibility, types of awards, recipient and NSF responsibilities, and organizational roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of participation by underrepresented/underserved groups
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF highly encourages the leadership, partnership, and contributions of individuals who are members of groups underrepresented and/or underserved in STEM education programs and careers in all NSF opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes leading and designing proposals; serving as peer reviewers, advisory committee members, committee of visitor members; and serving as NSF leadership, program, and administrative staff. NSF strongly promotes and expects equitable and inclusive treatment of such individuals in the Foundation’s proposal and award process, and encourages institutions that enroll and employ these individuals to lead, partner, and contribute to NSF opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research NSF funds (eligible/ineligible areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF funds research and education in most fields of science and engineering, but does not normally support certain activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF does not normally support: technical assistance, pilot plant efforts, research requiring security classification, development of products for commercial marketing, or market research for a particular project/invention. Biological research on mechanisms of disease in humans (etiology, diagnosis, treatment) is normally not supported, nor development of animal models or procedures for treatment—except where research advances knowledge in engineering, mathematical, physical, computer, or information sciences. Bioengineering and assistive information technology research to aid persons with disabilities is eligible. Consult program-specific solicitations and NSF 'Funding' and 'Awards' pages for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary proposals and proposer types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation considers proposals submitted by organizations on behalf of individuals or groups for support in most fields of research; interdisciplinary proposals are eligible for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are submitted by eligible organizations (see Chapter I.E). The term 'proposal' is interchangeable with 'application' for purposes of the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part I applicability and solicitation precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Part I of the PAPPG sets forth NSF’s proposal preparation and submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some NSF programs have program solicitations that modify the general provisions of the PAPPG; where a solicitation modifies the PAPPG the solicitation must be followed. When preparing and submitting proposals via Grants.gov, follow the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part II applicability and incorporation of federal regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Part II sets forth NSF policies/procedures regarding award, administration, and monitoring of grants and cooperative agreements and serves as NSF’s implementation of 2 CFR §200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PAPPG and award conditions are silent on an area covered by 2 CFR §200, the requirements in 2 CFR §200 must be followed. Part II also implements other applicable Public Laws and Executive Orders insofar as they apply to awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference into awards
rubrics_metrics.description: When NSF award general terms and conditions or an award notice reference a particular section of the PAPPG, that section becomes part of the award requirements through incorporation by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and recipients should treat referenced PAPPG sections as binding award requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAPPG non-applicability to NSF contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAPPG does not apply to NSF contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For information relating to NSF contracts consult the Guide to the NSF Contracting Process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance Listings / CFDA migration to SAM.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: The System for Award Management (SAM) provides public descriptions of Federal assistance listings and replaces CFDA.gov functionality; assistance listings continue to be associated with unique five-digit CFDA numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF program listings map to specific SAM assistance listings (e.g., 47.041 Engineering, 47.074 Biological Sciences, etc.). Use SAM.gov for assistance listing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Grant Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Grant Agreement is a legal instrument of financial assistance between NSF and a recipient that is used to transfer anything of value to carry out a public purpose authorized by law and is not to acquire property or services for NSF’s direct benefit or use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grant is distinguished from a cooperative agreement in that it does not provide for substantial NSF involvement in carrying out the activity. NSF makes Standard and Continuing Grants (see separate definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Grant vs Continuing Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Grant: NSF provides a specific level of support for a specified period with no statement of intent to provide additional future support. Continuing Grant: NSF provides initial support with a stated intent to provide additional support for additional periods, subject to funds availability and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct grant type when planning proposal budgets and timelines; terms affect expectations about future support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Cost Reimbursement Award
rubrics_metrics.description: A Cost Reimbursement Award reimburses the recipient for work performed and/or costs incurred up to the total amount specified in the award; such costs must be allowable in accordance with applicable cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability is based primarily on technical progress, financial accounting, and fiscal reporting. Except under certain programs/circumstances, NSF awards are normally cost reimbursement type awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Fixed Amount Award
rubrics_metrics.description: A Fixed Amount Award provides a specific level of support without regard to actual costs incurred under the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This award reduces administrative burden and recordkeeping; accountability is based primarily on performance and results. See 2 CFR §§200.102(c), 200.201(b), and 200.333 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Cooperative Agreement and substantial involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Cooperative Agreement is a legal instrument used to transfer value for a public purpose and is distinguished from a grant by providing for substantial NSF involvement in carrying out the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial involvement may be technical and/or managerial and can include NSF advice, review, approval, prior approvals of decisions/milestones, and more clearly defined deliverables. Use cooperative agreements when project objectives require extensive coordination with NSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of NSF involvement in cooperative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative agreements will specify the extent to which NSF will advise, review, approve or otherwise be involved with project activities, and NSF’s right to require more clearly defined deliverables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial involvement is incorporated in key accountability areas (prior agency approval requirements, type/frequency of project plans, special reporting requirements, project and recipient reviews). NSF may require prior approval of specific decisions, milestones, or project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient primary responsibility under cooperative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Under a cooperative agreement, the recipient has primary responsibility for conduct of the project; where NSF does not reserve responsibility for coordinating/integrating project activities, such responsibilities remain with the recipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While NSF will monitor in accordance with award terms, it will not assume overall control or unilaterally change project activities; the cooperative agreement will state specific areas of NSF involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of cooperative agreements: Standalone and Master/CSA
rubrics_metrics.description: Standalone Cooperative Agreement: a single unified award. Master Cooperative Agreement/Cooperative Support Agreement (CA/CSA): a master agreement with separately funded CSAs, each with its own award number and terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSAs have distinct award numbers and funding; no funding is attached to the master CA. CSAs contain specific terms in addition to the master agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of projects suitable for cooperative agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects suitable for cooperative agreements include management of research centers, large curriculum projects, multi-user facilities, projects involving complex subcontracting, construction or operations of major in-house university facilities, major instrumentation development, and projects where NSF participates with other stakeholder agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cooperative agreements for technically/managerially complex activities requiring extensive coordination between NSF and the recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of grants vs cooperative agreements (NSF-Recipient relationship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are used when accomplishment of project objectives requires minimal NSF involvement; cooperative agreements are used when substantial ongoing Foundation involvement is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under grants NSF provides specified financial support and monitors progress; recipients agree to perform the project as proposed, manage funds prudently, and carry out activities in accordance with award provisions (see Chapter VI.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative agreements for construction and MREFC funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative agreements for construction are generally funded through a separate MREFC appropriation and cannot be co-mingled with funds for activities other than construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF issues separate awards for operations and related activities; recipients must maintain accounting systems capable of segregating MREFC and operating costs and ensure such costs are applied accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Grants & Agreements (DGA) responsibilities and warrant authority
rubrics_metrics.description: DGA is responsible for award and administration of the majority of NSF’s assistance awards and conducts business, financial, and administrative reviews to ensure compliance with award terms and Federal rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants & Agreements Officers have delegated warrant authority to issue awards on behalf of the Foundation; their approval constitutes a legal obligation of Federal funds. They also issue award amendments, certain post-award prior approvals, monitor recipient compliance, and administer closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Institution & Award Support (DIAS) and Policy Office functions
rubrics_metrics.description: DIAS develops and implements proposal and award policies/procedures, clears funding opportunities, conducts advanced monitoring, cost analysis, audit resolution, electronic award systems administration, and outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Policy Office develops/coordinates issuance of pre- and post-award policies, provides guidance on interpretation of NSF policies, coordinates outreach and grants conferences, and advocates for research administration needs in NSF electronic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Analysis and Pre-award (CAP) Branch functions
rubrics_metrics.description: CAP specializes in determinations regarding allowability, allocability and reasonableness of costs either budgeted or claimed under NSF awards and evaluates accounting systems and internal controls of prospective/current recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAP conducts pre-award reviews of new recipients, Phase II small business projects, large-scale award budgets, and handles indirect cost rate negotiation; provides guidance to recipients on related questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution and Advanced Monitoring (RAM) Branch functions
rubrics_metrics.description: RAM determines allowability, allocability and reasonableness of costs claimed under NSF awards, evaluates recipient accounting systems and internal controls, and handles audit resolution and advanced monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary responsibilities include audit resolution, advanced monitoring to assess administrative capability/performance/compliance, and review of certain post-award expenditure adjustments; provides guidance to recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems Office responsibility for award business rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Systems Office designs, implements, administers, and oversees business rules for assistance awards across NSF electronic corporate systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is responsible for systems analysis and requirements development necessary for implementing award business rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Acquisition and Cooperative Support (DACS) roles
rubrics_metrics.description: DACS provides acquisition, contracts, other arrangements, and cooperative agreement award solutions and support; its Contracts Branch plans/solicits/negotiates/awards/administers contracts and the CSB handles cooperative agreements for major facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSB participates in integrated project teams, business process reviews, risk assessments, advanced cost analysis, oversight, and administrative assistance. DACS Policy Branch provides compliance oversight and operational policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Financial Management (DFM) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: DFM is responsible for financial policy and financial management of NSF, recipient business office relationships, and payment of vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Payments and Analytics Branch assists recipient financial and business officials with payment and financial reporting matters (see Chapter VIII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Facilities Office (LFO) oversight and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: LFO is the primary NSF resource for oversight practices related to mid-scale and major facility projects and the NSF-wide resource on project management best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LFO develops mandatory policies/procedures approved by senior management, provides expert assistance on non-scientific aspects of planning/budgeting/implementation, assures applicable requirements are followed, and fosters coordination to share lessons learned from prior major facility projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of the General Counsel (OGC) legal advisory role
rubrics_metrics.description: OGC is the legal advisor and advocate for the Foundation, providing legal advice/counsel on all aspects of Foundation programs, policies, and operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas include assistance awards and contracts; ethics and conflicts of interest; FOIA; Privacy Act; labor and personnel law; environmental law; Federal fiscal/administrative law; international law and agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Equity and Civil Rights (OECR) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: OECR administers NSF policies, practices and procedures related to external equal opportunity and civil rights, ensuring compliance with Federal-sector EEO and civil rights laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OECR fosters a diverse and inclusive work environment, conducts workforce analyses, outreach and education, responds to civil rights matters pertaining to NSF programs receiving federal assistance, and is the authority for receiving/processing notifications required by the Award Term 'Notification Requirements Regarding Sexual Harassment, Other Forms of Harassment, or Sexual Assault' (see Chapter XI.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Inspector General (OIG) oversight and investigative role
rubrics_metrics.description: OIG is an independent oversight office responsible for audits, reviews, and investigations of NSF programs and organizations/individuals that apply for or receive NSF funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG investigates allegations of research misconduct (plagiarism, falsification, fabrication) and program integrity/financial or nonfinancial wrongdoing, which can result in criminal, civil, or administrative sanctions; contact information and hotline provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility for conduct and publication of project results
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are wholly responsible for conducting their project activities and preparing results for publication; NSF does not assume responsibility for such findings or their interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must manage technical activities, reporting, and dissemination consistent with award terms; NSF’s role is stewardship and monitoring, not taking responsibility for research conclusions.
